claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent more than a hundred thousand years getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: Not reached: https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1992ApJ...401..759M/abstract (doi:10.1086/172103), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1023/A:1022952621810, https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1086/172103. The session's network policy refuses every host (proxy 403 on CONNECT, DNS not allowed for WebFetch), and the Firecrawl scrape was refused for lack of credits.
claims.note: The wording is built correctly for A3: 'more than a hundred thousand' is a lower bound that holds for both of the SOURCES' figures (Mitalas & Sills 1.7e5 yr photon diffusion; Stix ~3e7 yr energy-transport/Kelvin-Helmholtz). But I could not open either paper, so neither figure is confirmed. Pedant risk to weigh once the sources are read: Stix's 3e7 yr is a characteristic time scale (thermal content / luminosity), not a measured age of particular energy. 'Spent ... getting out' reads as an age, so check that the Stix abstract supports 'energy transport time' in those words.

claims.claim: What the first sentence alone leaves a viewer who swipes at second two believing: the energy (not the light) in sunlight took over 100,000 years to leave the Sun. (Visual meanwhile: a pulse crossing from Sun to Earth.)
claims.source_checked: script/age-of-sunlight.txt line 1; src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx line 199 (pulse frames 6-106). Cited papers not reached (see claim 1).
claims.note: A4 framing passes on the wording: the sentence avoids the popular false version ('the light is 100,000 years old') by making 'energy' the subject, and the pulse crossing during the hook shows the light trip, not a 100,000-year journey. Whether what the viewer leaves with is true rests on claim 1, which is unverified.

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.source_checked: Not reached: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?c (CODATA 2022 c); IAU 2012 Resolution B2 (iau.org). Both blocked by the session network policy.
claims.note: The arithmetic checks out from the values the SOURCES block states: 149,597,870,700 m / 299,792,458 m/s = 499.005 s = 8 min 19 s. For perihelion/aphelion (±1.67%) it is 8.18-8.46 min, so 'eight minutes' is fair rounding. But I could not open the IAU or NIST pages to confirm the two constants, so the claim is not confirmed by an opened source.

claims.claim: Getting out was the slow part.
claims.source_checked: No new source; rests on claims 1 and 3.
claims.note: Follows if claims 1 and 3 hold (more than 1e5 yr against about 8 min). Both are unverified, so this is too.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light.
claims.source_checked: Not reached: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml; https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (both refused by the session network policy).
claims.note: SOURCES entry 4 cites two A2 agency pages, so A1/A2 are met on paper. But I could not open either page to check the paraphrases attributed to them ('mostly gamma rays and X-rays', 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light', 'absorbed and re-emitted repeatedly').

This is an absolute, and SOURCES entry 4 gets to it by inference ('So the light that leaves the surface is not the light made in the core') from 'absorbed and re-emitted repeatedly' plus the convective outer 30%. When the pages can be read, check that they support the absolute and not only 'most'. Pedant risk: in the deep interior much of the opacity is electron (Thomson) scattering, where a photon is scattered rather than absorbed. The convection-zone hand-off (no radiative path above ~0.7 R) is the stronger basis for 'no photon', and the SOURCES entry should say so explicitly.

claims.source_checked: No new source; rests on claim 1 (papers not reached).
claims.note: True under either figure the SOURCES give (1.7e5 or ~3e7 yr), but neither was opened.

claims.claim: The light is eight minutes old.
claims.note: Same arithmetic as claim 3 (about 8.3 min from the photosphere, where the light was last emitted). The sources were not opened.

claims.source_checked: src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx line 334; IAU/NIST pages not reached.
claims.note: Same as claim 3. 'Surface' (photosphere) is the right starting point for the 499 s figure.

claims.claim: 100,000+ YEARS / energy, core to surface / not one photon · not to scale
claims.source_checked: src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx line 337; Mitalas & Sills (bibcode 1992ApJ...401..759M) and Stix (doi:10.1023/A:1022952621810) not reached.
claims.note: Matches the spoken lower bound and correctly labels the cutaway as energy, not one photon, and as not to scale (A6). The figure itself is unverified (see claim 1).

claims.claim: Sun and Earth drawn side by side, with a bright pulse crossing the gap between them
claims.source_checked: src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx line 42 (Sun r=110, Earth r=24, centres 600 apart) and lines 199-201 (pulse); script/age-of-sunlight.txt (spoken lines and SOURCES).
claims.note: A6: as drawn, Earth is 0.22 of the Sun's radius and the gap is about 5.5 solar radii. The real figures are about 1/109 of the Sun's radius and about 215 solar radii (standard values, not re-sourced here because no source could be opened). The pulse crosses in about 3 s for an 8-minute trip. That makes this a deliberately non-to-scale visual, but the only 'not to scale' on screen is on the 100,000+ YEARS tag, which belongs to the interior cutaway (line 337), and the script never says it. Fix: add 'not to scale' to this shot, e.g. 8 MINUTES / 'surface to your skin · not to scale', and to the closing return to this shot under THE ENERGY / THE LIGHT. Alternatively, have the VO say it.

claims.claim: Sun cutaway with rings at 0.25 R (core) and 0.7 R (base of the radiative zone / top of convection zone)
claims.note: The SOURCES give 0.25/0.70 (NASA MSFC) and 0.713 R (Christensen-Dalsgaard, Gough & Thompson 1991), both A2 citations, and 0.7 is fair rounding of 0.713 under 'not to scale'. Neither source could be opened.

claims.claim: A random-walk path from the centre out to the 0.7 ring, with short side-stubs along it (repeated absorption and re-emission through the radiative zone)
claims.note: The shape is labelled on screen as 'energy', 'not one photon' and 'not to scale' (A6 labelling met). The underlying claim (energy random-walks through the radiative zone by absorption and re-emission) is attributed to NASA SVS/MSFC, which could not be opened.

claims.claim: Path colour shifts from violet ('gamma' in code) near the core to pale yellow ('visible') reached exactly at the 0.7 ring
claims.source_checked: src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx lines 117-126 (tint: t = r / RADIATIVE, so the colour is fully VISIBLE at r = 0.7); script SOURCES entries 4 and 6.
claims.note: The visual contradicts the script's own sources as the SOURCES block reports them. Entry 4 says NASA MSFC has the energy 'ultimately leave the surface as visible light', and the code comment above tint says 'visible light by the surface', yet tint() completes the shift at 0.7 R, the bottom of the convection zone. Radiation there is at roughly 2 million K, soft X-ray, not visible; it becomes visible only at the photosphere. Fix: end the ramp short of the visible colour at 0.7 (e.g. scale t by r/1.0, or stop at a mid violet-blue), and let pale yellow appear only in the surface ray fan. Also, the radiation field in the core at about 15 MK is thermal X-ray; fusion gamma rays are thermalised almost at once. So SOURCES entry 6's 'from gamma to visible' should read 'from X-ray (gamma at birth) to visible', or be backed by whatever MSFC actually says. Not on screen as a word, so this part is a SOURCES accuracy point. Re-check against MSFC once it can be read.

claims.claim: Rotating convection cells fill the shell from 0.7 R to the surface (energy carried by convection, not radiation, in the outer ~30%)
claims.note: The SOURCES cite NASA MSFC ('convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface'), an A2 source, but the page could not be opened.

claims.claim: A fan of five yellow light rays leaves the surface (energy leaves the photosphere as visible light)
claims.note: Matches SOURCES entry 4's reading of NASA MSFC ('ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'), which could not be opened. Strictly, sunlight leaving the photosphere spans UV to IR with most of the energy in visible and near-IR; pale yellow is acceptable shorthand under 'not to scale'.
